title: Fullstack: Vite React (SSR-ready) + NestJS API implementing JWT + OAuth2 (Google/GitHub) + Organization onboarding
summary: Added a NestJS backend implementing JWT authentication, OAuth2 (Google and GitHub via Passport), and organization onboarding endpoints. Added a Vite React frontend (SSR-ready structure) with Material UI pages for Login and Organization Onboarding, a nanostores-based auth store, and a small API client to interact with the backend.
thoughtProcess: Provide a minimal, pragmatic, and type-safe scaffold that integrates Prisma data models (user, account, password, organization, session) with NestJS auth flows (email/password -> JWT, OAuth callbacks via Passport) and a Vite + React frontend that consumes the API. Kept service boundaries clear: PrismaService for DB access, AuthService for credential verification, JwtStrategy for protected routes, Passport strategies for Google/GitHub. Frontend uses nanostores for client-side auth state, simple MUI forms for login and onboarding, and a small api client handling token storage. Focused on correctness of types and idiomatic structure; left environment variable names obvious for developer setup (e.g., GOOGLE\_CLIENT\_ID, JWT\_SECRET).
documentation:
### Overview
This patch provides a working scaffold implementing the requested features:

- **Backend (NestJS)**
  - JWT authentication with email/password.
  - OAuth2 sign-in using Passport strategies (Google and GitHub).
  - Organization onboarding endpoints for creating organizations and listing a user's organizations.
  - PrismaService to access the PostgreSQL database described by user's Prisma models.

- **Frontend (Vite + React)**
  - `Login` page supports email/password login and buttons to start OAuth flows.
  - `Onboarding` page lets an authenticated user create an Organization.
  - `authStore` (nanostores) holds auth state and token and is used to gate onboarding.
  - `api.ts` centralizes API calls and token handling.

### Environment variables (backend)
- DATABASE\_URL
- JWT\_SECRET
- JWT\_EXPIRES\_IN (e.g.

)
- GOOGLE\_CLIENT\_ID
- GOOGLE\_CLIENT\_SECRET
- GITHUB\_CLIENT\_ID
- GITHUB\_CLIENT\_SECRET
- OAUTH\_CALLBACK\_BASE\_URL (e.g., [https://api.example.com/auth/oauth)
-](https://api.example.com/auth/oauth%29
-) FRONTEND\_BASE\_URL (frontend base e.g., [http://localhost:5173)

###](http://localhost:5173%29

###) Notes & Next Steps
- Configure Passport session usage if you prefer cookie-based session flows for OAuth; this example uses stateless JWTs emitted after OAuth success.
- Add validation pipes and stronger DTO validation rules (class-validator) before production.
- Add rate-limiting on auth endpoints and email verification flow for security.
- Add proper SSR hydration on frontend (this scaffold is SSR-ready structure; implementing full Vite SSR entry/server is left as next step).

### Dependencies (recommended additions to package.json)
**Backend**:
- @nestjs/common, @nestjs/core, @nestjs/passport, @nestjs/jwt, passport, passport-google-oauth20, passport-github2, passport-jwt, bcrypt, prisma, @prisma/client

**Frontend**:
- react, react-dom, @nanostores/react, @nanostores/core, @mui/material (v7+), @mui/icons-material (v7+), axios, react-router-dom (if routing added)

(Include dependency additions in your project manifest as appropriate.)
